questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: One of the most important aspects for me was the language and academic opportunities. I am personally very interested in further studying or working abroad someday, why it seemed like an exceptional opportunity to go to England. Likewise, I wanted to be able to experience a different approach to the academics and I wanted to expand my social network.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
The Erasmus team at Kent were very helpful with most issues, questions or inquiries. They were also fairly quick to respond to emails, although it could take a little longer at times. However, some things were not stated explicitly anywhere, so you had to spend some time to search for some things on Kent's website. The majority of information is also available of KU's website.

The only thing that was a bit unsure, was the information concerning covid, particularly the covid-rules for arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. This should have been better and more organised.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
There were plenty of options to suit most budgets. You could prioritise which accommodation you wanted and I was fortunate enough to get what I had as my first choice. I had an en-suite bedroom in Keynes Flats (moderate living). My experience was, that this was one of the best places to live on campus (it is newer and more modern than some places on campus).

However, it is important to point out that I studied at Kent as part of my bachelor's degree/undergraduate, and I am not sure the same housing is available for post-graduate students/master's.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I chose self-catered accommodation, which meant I shared a kitchen with seven other flatmates. Luckily, my flatmates were very neat and clean, but unfortunately I experienced that this wasn't the case in some of the other flats.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That the cleanliness in the kitchens very much depends on the people you live with. Otherwise, I was very satisfied.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process took some time because you needed approval of several documents, which took time. Both KU and Kent were pleasant to be in contact with during this process. You may discover a lot of useful information on 'Udlandsrejser' on KU's website. Further, don't hesitate to contact the Erasmus team at Kent as they will help to guide you through the process as well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email - KU and Kent. And information on both their websites.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Three of my four modules were approved. The Erasmus Teams sent me a list of available modules from which I could select the last one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to contact the Erasmus team or KU. They will gladly help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Personally, I thought it was the same level as in KU - maybe a little easier. But I should also note, that I am fluent in English. I heard that some fellow exchange students found the language a little challenging. 

I had four seminars and four lectures each week. The seminars and lectures are only an hour long, so it is shorter than at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Because the seminars were shorter, there was less time to discuss and go over the material. So it was up to you to read most of it on beforehand. The professors, on the other hand, expect you to have completed the readings and to participate in the seminars. Another difference was the exams. They vary from module to module, but I had a lot of essays which was different from the 4 hour exams we have at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Law and International Development
Environmental Law
International Human Rights in Context
Privacy, Data Protection and Cybersecurity

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Privacy, Data Protection and Cybersecurity was by far my favourite module. It is very relevant and is something that keeps transforming as the world develops. I also have a personal interest in this area, why I found it even more interesting. 

All the other courses were also decent and the professors were competent. However, International Law and Development was not very law oriented.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing. Just be aware that public transport in England is quite expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
It was what I expected. In general less expensive than Denmark.
The accommodation was quite expensive, but it is possible to get a cheaper place on campus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: University of Kent has a lot of societies. Don't be afraid to join them! They are very sociable and you meet a lot of new people!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Societies!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It is easy to travel a lot of places from Kent as there is a train station a coach station near by. It is about 50 minutes from London, which is definitely worth a trip. Otherwise, I would recommend exploring the Kent area (by the coast), Brighton, Cambridge or Oxford.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have relatives in England and know the country and culture quite well. So I found fit quite easy to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies - this is definitely the place to meet people. Otherwise, talk and socialise with you flatmates (if you live on campus) and reach out to other international/exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open-minded
Don't be afraid to approach people
Be positive

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some students, especially first-year students, will be likely be younger than you. However, don't be put off by this. The majority of them are incredibly friendly, and suddenly age doesn't seem to matter.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people, learning a lot of new things about myself and gaining new knowledge.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing the work-load and social life. And dealing with a messy kitchen at times.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
